By Caroline Allen

Some UK-based funds are still hanging on in the US market despite warnings of an imminent correction, while others have sharply cut exposure, a monthly asset allocation survey of 15 fund groups by Reuters shows.
The survey sought participants' recommended portfolios for a global equity, global bond and UK pension fund in December.
In the global equity fund, the average US/Canada weighting among participants was barely changed at 25.2 percent of the portfolio from 25 percent a month ago.
UK and Germany were slightly lower, alongside a drop to 13 percent from 16 percent in the "Europe Other" equity category.
Japan showed only a slight easing but the Asia weighting leapt to 11.9 percent in December from nine percent in November.

Emerging markets interest was also higher, up nearly one percentage point to an average 2.9 percent, while cash was significantly higher, at 5.2 percent in December from 3.6 percent in November and 2.8 percent in October.
Contributor Nomura was heavily underweight US/Canada at 20.5 percent of the fund against its benchmark 46.5 percent.

The balance was absorbed by overweighting most other asset classes, including the UK at 17 percent against the benchmark 12 percent, Japan at 20 percent against 17.3 percent and Emerging Markets at 14 percent against the benchmark 5.5 percent.

Strategist Joe Rooney at Lehman Brothers has also cut his US weighting in December and raised exposure to the UK. Lehman also recommends 14 percent of the equity portfolio be invested in Emerging Markets and 23 percent in Japan.
But the Goldman Sachs global equity portfolio held 40 percent in US/Canada and Lombard Odier 43 percent.

Some funds have built up big cash holdings -- the ING Baring global equity fund had 12.4 percent, Kleinwort 15 percent and Regent Fund Management 18 percent. In the global bond portfolio, the average US, Canada, Japan and UK weightings were all up in December from the previous month, at the expense of Europe. Germany was slightly higher at an average 10.7 percent from 10.5 percent but overall Europe fell to 18.8 percent from 24.9 percent of the portfolio.
Cash in this category declined to an average 2.9 percent in December from 3.9 percent, against October's 2.1 percent.

Amongst contributors, Lombard Odier and Danske Invest had over 30 percent in non-core Europe, in contrast to BZW which had just 0.4 percent. BZW has 51.6 percent of its global bond fund in the US. Lombard also held 15 percent of its fund in cash.
Holdings in the UK pension fund portfolio showed funds had bought more UK equities in the past month, with the average weighting at 57 percent from 55.6 percent in November.

Contributors were also holding more UK gilts, with the average at 7.4 from 6.7 percent. Index-linked exposure, an indicator of funds' views on inflation, was up at 1.5 percent of the portfolio from 0.4 percent previously.

Average cash holdings eased from 5.8 percent in November to 4.5 percent this month, while holdings in the "Other" category, described by participants as property or commodity plays, rose to 2.8 percent from 2.3 percent.

Lehman and LGT had some of the heaviest weightings in UK equities at 70 percent and 60 percent respectively, but Lehman had just 16 percent for overseas equities against the average 24.3 percent for December.

Nomura's gilt holdings outstripped most other contributors at 12 percent of the fund, with the average for December at 7.4 percent. It also allocated five percent to index-linked bonds (average 1.5 percent) and held five percent cash.
